title: Lagos Seeks Africa-Wide Bioshield Alliance As Experts Advocate Stronger Surveillance, Research - Independent Newspaper Nigeria

analysis.time: The Lagos State Bioshield initiative was unveiled on November 25, 2026, with the conference held on November 24, 2026. The pilot deployment during CANEX WKND monitored delegates over 21 days.
analysis.location_and_population: Lagos, Nigeria, with an estimated population of about 30.1 million and an average population density of approximately 6,800 persons per square kilometre.
analysis.event: Lagos State Government unveiled a digital biosecurity framework called the Lagos State Bioshield to combat emerging infectious disease threats, including Lassa fever, dengue, yellow fever, Marburg virus disease, and Ebola, as well as genetically modified and unknown pathogens. The initiative was reported by the Independent Newspaper Nigeria.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The pilot deployment during CANEX WKND monitored approximately 19,000 registered delegates, including 2,298 international visitors. The system recorded 2,454 telemedicine consultations, 241 clinical referrals, and 219 individuals flagged for further attention. No severe outcomes were associated with the suspected high-consequence infections reported.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The Lagos State Bioshield is currently in operation, with plans for an upgraded version (Bioshield 3.0) to enhance AI and telemedicine capabilities, integrate with airports and event venues, and establish sustainable financing and legal frameworks. The system is designed to monitor and respond to biological threats without disrupting economic activities.

analysis.brief_en: Lagos State Government has launched the Lagos State Bioshield, a digital biosecurity framework aimed at detecting, monitoring, and containing emerging infectious disease threats. The initiative, unveiled on November 25, 2026, integrates artificial intelligence, telemedicine, and digital health surveillance to ensure public health protection without disrupting economic activities. The framework was developed from lessons learned during the Ebola outbreak and the COVID-19 pandemic, emphasizing the need to balance health security with economic sustainability. The pilot deployment during the CANEX WKND event monitored 19,000 delegates, including 2,298 international visitors, and recorded 2,454 telemedicine consultations, 241 clinical referrals, and 219 individuals flagged for further attention. No severe outcomes were linked to the suspected high-consequence infections. The system is designed to identify potential biological threats associated with people entering Lagos and monitor individuals for symptoms. It also uses AI to classify risks and escalate cases to relevant authorities within 24 hours. The initiative includes plans for Bioshield 3.0, which will enhance technology, integrate with airports and event venues, and establish sustainable financing and legal frameworks. The system is part of a broader effort to strengthen Africa’s health security through the One Health approach, which considers human, animal, and environmental health as interconnected.

analysis.time: The training and orientation programme was conducted on November 26, 2026, with the first session focusing on community-based surveillance and risk communication, and a subsequent session planned for the management of suspected cases.
analysis.location_and_population: The event took place in Makurdi, Benue State, Nigeria, involving approximately 30 participants, including community engagement personnel, state surveillance focal persons, and representatives from public and private health facilities.
analysis.event: Benue State Government intensified preparedness against a possible outbreak of Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) by training health workers and journalists on early detection, surveillance, risk communication, and safe referral of suspected cases. The training was organized with support from the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control (NCDC).
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: No suspected cases of Ebola were recorded in Benue State. However, the state had already reported suspected and confirmed cases of Lassa fever. The training aimed to strengthen preparedness and response capacity, with no reported symptoms among monitored travelers.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The training was part of a preparedness measure, with no confirmed outbreak. The state epidemiologist monitors travelers from high-risk countries for 2 to 21 days. The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control (NCDC) issued an alert to states following reports of Ebola cases in Nigeria.

analysis.brief_en: Benue State in Nigeria has intensified its preparedness against a potential Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) outbreak by training health workers and journalists on early detection, surveillance, and risk communication. The training, organized with support from the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control (NCDC), aimed to strengthen the state’s response capacity following reports of Ebola cases in Nigeria. The State Disease Surveillance and Notification Officer, Aluga Doosuur Maureen, emphasized that no suspected cases of Ebola had been recorded in Benue, and the exercise was strictly a preparedness measure. The state has also implemented a monitoring mechanism for travelers from high-risk countries, tracking them for up to 21 days to detect any symptoms. No reported symptoms were found among monitored individuals. Additionally, the state is focusing on Lassa fever, which has already seen suspected and confirmed cases. The training included community-based surveillance and safe referral procedures, with a follow-up session planned for case managers. The World Health Organisation (WHO) representative noted the importance of integrating disease surveillance efforts, highlighting the need for vigilance against viral haemorrhagic fevers, including Ebola and Lassa fever.

source_language_evidence.scale_impact_and_risk: VLPdEm5 mRNA-LNP诱导高水平广交叉结合抗体(VLPdEm5 mRNA-LNP elicits high-level and broadly cross-reactive binding antibody responses in mice):mRNA-LNP day28 ED50均值471,day56均值8862;质粒-LNP低剂量后结合抗体延迟出现;day70 mRNA-LNP弱中和NT50约1:30–1:70,质粒-LNP未检测到;day70血清结合六个LASV谱系GPC。
source_language_evidence.brief_en: 今日动态 返回首页 会员注册 登录 生物通快讯免费订阅 首页 今日动态 人才市场 新技术专栏 中国科学人 云展台 BioHot 定制我的BioHot 进入我的BioHot 进入我的集采 肿瘤癌症研究 免疫/基因/细胞疗法 神经生物学 健康与疾病 衰老机制与长寿 单细胞技术 基因编辑-CRISPR RNA研究 肠道菌与人体微生态 细胞代谢 AI生物信息学 COVID 云讲堂直播 会展中心 特价专栏 技术快讯 免费试用 生物通官微 陪你抓住生命科技 跳动的脉搏 生物通首页 > 今日动态 > 正文 ESCRT工程化mRNA-VLP疫苗通过赋予拉沙病毒(LASV)GPC自主出芽能力诱导体液与细胞免疫 《Virologica Sinica》:An ESCRT-engineered mRNA-VLP vaccine elicits humoral and cellular immunity against Lassa virus 【字体: 大 中 小 】 时间:2026年11月27日 来源:Virologica Sinica 4.7 编辑推荐: 拉沙病毒(Lassa virus,LASV)在西非引起严重出血热,但目前尚无获批疫苗。LASV抗原设计的主要障碍在于,其唯一中和靶点糖蛋白复合物(glycoprotein complex,GPC)缺乏内在晚期结构域(late-domain)基序,无法招募宿主E 为了促进科学的传播,生物通采集了这篇文章 订阅BioHot点这里解锁原文链接推送! “畅读会员”点此登录查看原文链接 Open access 拉沙病毒(Lassa virus,LASV)在西非引起严重出血热,但目前尚无获批疫苗。LASV抗原设计的主要障碍在于,其唯一中和靶点糖蛋白复合物(glycoprotein complex,GPC)缺乏内在晚期结构域(late-domain)基序,无法招募宿主ESCRT(endosomal sorting complex required for transport)机制以完成颗粒释放。在此,研究人员报告一种理性设计策略:通过在LASV GPC胞质域末端附加合成的ESCRT招募盒(ESCRT-recruitment cassette),赋予其自主出芽能力。对由16个构建体组成的矩阵进行系统筛选,鉴定出先导候选VLPdEm5。该构建体整合ESCRT招募盒、优化的弗林蛋白酶(furin)切割位点以及异源H1N1跨膜-胞质域(transmembrane-cytoplasmic domain),以支持高效颗粒组装和构象中和表位的正确展示。通过脂质纳米颗粒包封的mRNA(lipid-nanoparticle-encapsulated mRNA,mRNA-LNP)递送,VLPdEm5驱动高效原位病毒样颗粒(virus-like particle。

title: Oyo govt intensifies fumigation of public spaces to prevent Ebola, others - Tribune Online

analysis.time: Sign In Follow US Metro Oyo govt intensifies fumigation of public spaces to prevent Ebola, others Busola Oworu November 24, 2026 Share Add as a preferred source Oyo State Government has intensified fumigation and disinfection of strategic public spaces across the state as part of efforts to prevent the spread of infectious diseases, including Ebola and Lassa fever.
analysis.location_and_population: This was contained in a statement released by the Commissioner for Information, Prince Dotun Oyelade, who said that the Commissioner for Environment and Natural Resources, Ademola Aderinto, disclosed this during a fumigation and disinfection exercise at selected locations in Ibadan.
analysis.event: Oyo State Government intensifies fumigation and disinfection of public spaces to prevent the spread of infectious diseases, including Ebola and Lassa fever. The government is taking proactive steps to guard against the possible introduction and spread of infectious diseases.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The exercise covers several strategic public spaces, including Ibadan Airport, Mapo Hall, and markets. The government will sustain the fumigation and disinfection programme to ensure public spaces remain safe.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The government is taking proactive measures to prevent the spread of infectious diseases. No confirmed cases of Ebola have been recorded in Oyo State.

analysis.brief_en: Oyo State Government in Nigeria has intensified fumigation and disinfection of public spaces like Ibadan Airport and markets to prevent the spread of infectious diseases, including Ebola and Lassa fever. The government is taking proactive steps to ensure public safety, despite no confirmed cases of Ebola in the state.
analysis.summary_en: Oyo State Government in Nigeria has intensified fumigation and disinfection of public spaces like Ibadan Airport and markets to prevent the spread of infectious diseases, including Ebola and Lassa fever. The government is taking proactive steps to ensure public safety, despite no confirmed cases of Ebola in the state.
